syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

topics.title: Role of Business in the Development of the Economy

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how indigenous instruments such as hundi and chitties helped the transfer of money for trade.
Describe the trade centres, exports and favourable balance of trade that made ancient India prosperous.
Explain how India's economy changed under British rule, after independence and with the reforms of 1991.
Distinguish economic activities from non-economic activities by their motive.
Identify the characteristics that distinguish a business activity from other activities.

topics.title: Comparison of Business, Profession and Employment

concepts.learning_objective: Compare business, profession and employment on mode of establishment, qualification and reward.
Compare business, profession and employment on capital, risk and transfer of interest.
Classify extractive and genetic industries as primary industries with examples.
Classify manufacturing (analytical, synthetical, processing, assembling) and construction industries.
Explain why tertiary industries provide support services and form part of commerce.

topics.title: Commerce, Trade and Auxiliaries to Trade

concepts.learning_objective: Relate each activity of commerce to the hindrance of persons, place, time, risk, finance or information it removes.
Explain the role of transport, banking, insurance, warehousing, advertising and public relations in trade.
Explain why profit is an essential but not the only objective of business.
Identify the multiple objectives of business such as market standing, innovation, productivity and social responsibility.
Distinguish speculative risks from pure risks with examples.
Explain the nature of business risks, including profit as the reward for risk taking.
Classify the causes of business risks into natural, human, economic and other causes.
Explain the meaning of entrepreneurship and its role in the economic development of a nation.
Identify the basic factors an entrepreneur must consider while starting a business.
Describe the features of sole proprietorship, including unlimited liability and the absence of a separate entity.
Explain the merits and limitations of sole proprietorship and relate them to business situations.
Describe the formation, membership, control and liability of a Joint Hindu family business.
Explain the merits and limitations of a Joint Hindu family business.
Explain the features of partnership such as unlimited joint liability, mutual agency and the number of partners.
Explain the merits and limitations of the partnership form of organisation.
Distinguish between active, sleeping, secret and nominal partners, partners by estoppel and holding out, and a minor admitted to benefits.
Classify partnerships by duration and by liability and state the features of each type.
State the purpose and the usual contents of a partnership deed.
Explain the procedure of registering a partnership firm and the consequences of non-registration.
Explain the features, merits and limitations of a cooperative society.
Identify the type of cooperative society from its members, aims and working.

topics.title: Joint stock company and its types

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the features, merits and limitations of a joint stock company, including limited liability.
Distinguish between a private company and a public company and state the privileges of a private company.

topics.title: Choice of form of business organisation

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the factors that determine the choice of form and the form most advantageous on each.
Evaluate which form of organisation suits a given business as its scale and needs change.

topics.title: Private sector, public sector and the mixed economy

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why the Indian economy is called a mixed economy and identify the forms of private sector organisation.
Describe the public sector and the features of public ownership, public funds and public accountability.
Trace how the Industrial Policy Resolutions of 1948 and 1956 and the 1991 policy defined the roles of the two sectors.
State the features of departmental undertakings as the oldest form of public enterprise.
Evaluate the merits and limitations of departmental undertakings.
Explain the features of statutory corporations created by a Special Act of Parliament.
Evaluate the merits and limitations of statutory corporations.
Define a government company under Section 2(45) of the Companies Act, 2013.
Explain the features, merits and limitations of government companies.

topics.title: Changing role of the public sector

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the role of the public sector in infrastructure, regional balance, economies of scale, checking concentration of economic power and import substitution.
Describe the 1991 reforms: fewer reserved industries, disinvestment, policy on sick units and the MoU system.
Identify the features of global enterprises such as huge capital resources, advanced technology, product innovation and marketing strategies.
Explain centralised control, expansion of market territory and foreign collaboration by global enterprises.

topics.title: Joint ventures and public private partnership

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish between contractual and equity-based joint ventures.
Explain the benefits of joint ventures.
Describe the public private partnership model, its features, strengths and weaknesses.

topics.title: Nature of services and their difference from goods

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the five Is of services: intangibility, inconsistency, inseparability, inventory (less) and involvement.
Distinguish services from goods on the basis of nature, type and the five Is.

topics.title: Types of services and business services

concepts.learning_objective: Classify services into business, social and personal services with examples.
Identify the specialised business services that enterprises depend on and explain why.

topics.title: Banking: types of banks and functions of commercial banks

concepts.learning_objective: Describe commercial, cooperative, specialised and central banks.
Explain the functions of commercial banks, including deposits, lending, cheques, remittance and allied services.
Explain the concept of e-banking and the range of services it offers.
Explain the benefits of e-banking to customers and to banks.
Explain the fundamental principle and functions of insurance.
Apply the principles of insurance such as utmost good faith, indemnity, contribution and mitigation.

topics.title: Types of insurance: life, fire and marine

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the types of life insurance policies and the needs each one meets.
Explain the elements of fire and marine insurance and compare them with life insurance.
Describe the financial, mail and allied facilities offered by postal services.
Describe the types of telecom services available to business.
Explain the importance of transportation as a business service.
Describe private, public, bonded, government and cooperative warehouses.
Explain the functions of warehousing such as consolidation, break the bulk, stock piling and financing.
Identify the trends shaping business and the factors behind the emerging modes of business.
Distinguish e-business from e-commerce in terms of the functions each covers.

topics.title: Scope of e-business: B2B, B2C, intra-B and C2C

concepts.learning_objective: Explain business-to-business transactions and the use of networks with suppliers and distributors.
Describe B2C commerce as a wide range of marketing activities and its C2B corollary.
Explain intra-B commerce within a firm and C2C commerce between consumers with its safeguards.
Compare traditional and e-business on ease of formation, location, set-up cost and operating cost.
Compare traditional and e-business on structure, process cycle, personal touch, pre-sampling and risk.
Explain the benefits of e-business such as ease of formation, convenience, speed, global reach and paperless working.
Identify e-business applications such as e-procurement, e-bidding, e-delivery and e-trading.
Explain the limitations of e-business such as low personal touch, digital divide, risk and people resistance.
Explain how the limitations of e-business are being overcome.
Describe the stages of an online transaction from registration to delivery.
Distinguish the payment mechanisms used in online shopping.
Identify default on order, delivery and payment, and the safeguards against them.
Explain viruses, hacking and cryptography as data storage and transmission concerns.
Explain the risks to intellectual property and privacy once information is online.

chapters.title: Social Responsibilities of Business and Business Ethics

topics.title: Concept of social responsibility and CSR

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the meaning of social responsibility of business and identify socially desirable practices.
Distinguish social responsibility from legal responsibility.
Apply the CSR provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 described in the chapter.

topics.title: Arguments for and against social responsibility

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the arguments in favour of business assuming social responsibilities.
Explain the arguments against business assuming social responsibilities.
Identify the forces that have made business concerned with social responsibility.

topics.title: Kinds of social responsibility and responsibility towards interest groups

concepts.learning_objective: Classify business actions as economic, legal, ethical or discretionary responsibility.
Describe the responsibilities of business towards shareholders, workers, consumers, government and community.
Define environment and pollution and explain why pollution exists.
Identify air, water, land and noise pollution caused by business activities.

topics.title: Pollution control and role of business in environmental protection

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the reasons that make a case for pollution control by business.
Describe the steps a business enterprise can take to protect the environment.
Explain the concept of business ethics and its relationship with law and profits.
Identify the basic elements through which an enterprise fosters ethics.

topics.title: Stages in the formation of a company

concepts.learning_objective: Name the three stages in the formation of a company in their proper order and identify the promoters who carry them out.
Explain why a private company does not need the capital subscription stage while a public company raising public funds does.

topics.title: Promotion and the functions of a promoter

concepts.learning_objective: State who is a promoter under section 69 and distinguish promoters from professionals who merely assist them.
Distinguish between technical, financial and economic feasibility of a business opportunity.
Explain how a company's name is approved and when a proposed name is considered undesirable.

topics.title: Memorandum of Association and its clauses

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why the Memorandum of Association is the most important document of a company.
Identify the contents of the name, registered office and objects clauses of the Memorandum.
Apply the liability and capital clauses to calculate a member's liability and the limit on share issues.

topics.title: Articles of Association and other documents for registration
topics.ncert_sections: 7.2.1 (Documents required to be submitted: B to F)

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the Articles of Association as rules of internal management subsidiary to the Memorandum.
Identify the consent of directors, agreement, statutory declaration and fee receipt filed for registration.
Distinguish between the Memorandum and the Articles of Association on objectives, position and validity of acts.

topics.title: Legal position of promoters and preliminary contracts

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the fiduciary position of promoters, their liability and their right to expenses and remuneration.
Explain what preliminary contracts are and who is bound by them.

topics.title: Incorporation and the Certificate of Incorporation

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the application for incorporation, the documents filed with it and the role of the Registrar.
Explain the effect of the Certificate of Incorporation as conclusive evidence of a company's legal existence.
Explain the meaning of a prospectus and the need for SEBI approval before raising funds from the public.
Apply the 90 per cent minimum subscription rule to decide whether shares can be allotted.
Describe the stock exchange application, allotment of shares and filing of the return of allotment.

topics.title: Meaning, nature and significance of business finance

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the meaning of business finance and why finance is called the life blood of business.
Identify fixed capital requirements and the factors that change their size.
Explain working capital requirements and why they differ between businesses.
Classify sources of funds into long-term, medium-term and short-term sources by period.
Distinguish between owner's funds and borrowed funds.
Distinguish between internal and external sources of funds.

topics.title: Retained earnings, trade credit and factoring

concepts.learning_objective: Evaluate the merits and limitations of retained earnings as a source of finance.
Explain trade credit as a short-term source and assess its merits and limitations.
Describe factoring services and distinguish between recourse and non-recourse factoring.

topics.title: Lease financing, public deposits and commercial paper

concepts.learning_objective: Explain lease financing and evaluate its merits and limitations for the lessee.
Describe public deposits and evaluate them as a source of finance.
Explain the features of commercial paper and who can raise funds through it.
Explain equity shares and evaluate them as a source of long-term finance.
Explain the preferential rights and types of preference shares.

topics.title: Debentures, commercial banks and financial institutions

concepts.learning_objective: Explain debentures and evaluate their merits and limitations as borrowed capital.
Evaluate loans from commercial banks as a source of finance.
Explain the role of financial institutions (development banks) in business finance.
Identify international commercial banks, agencies and development banks as sources of funds.
Distinguish between GDRs, ADRs and IDRs.
Explain the features of foreign currency convertible bonds.

topics.title: Factors affecting the choice of the source of funds

concepts.learning_objective: Match the source of funds with the purpose and period for which funds are needed.
Evaluate sources of funds in terms of risk and their effect on control of owners.
Explain how cost, tax benefits and the form of organisation affect the choice of source.
Describe the contribution of MSMEs to production, employment, exports and the value chain of the Indian economy.
Classify an enterprise as micro, small or medium using investment in plant and machinery and turnover, and recall the MSMED Act, 2006.
Explain the meaning of village industries and cottage industries.
Explain why MSMEs, being labour intensive, are vital employers in a labour-surplus country like India.
Explain how MSMEs promote balanced regional development using local resources.
Identify the advantages of MSMEs such as low cost of production, entrepreneurship opportunity and quick decision making.
Analyse the problems of finance and procurement of raw materials faced by MSMEs.
Explain the problems of managerial skills and marketing faced by small businesses.
Analyse the problems of quality, capacity utilisation and global competition faced by MSMEs.
State the meaning of entrepreneurship, entrepreneur and enterprise and the need for entrepreneurship.
Identify the characteristics of entrepreneurship such as systematic, lawful activity, innovation and organisation of production.
Explain why entrepreneurial risk is a calculated risk.

topics.title: Intellectual property rights: meaning and importance

concepts.learning_objective: Define intellectual property and distinguish between industrial property and copyright.
Explain traditional knowledge, the TKDL and trade secrets as forms of intellectual property.
Explain why IPR is important for entrepreneurs and creators.

topics.title: Types of IP: copyright, trademark and geographical indication

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the meaning and features of copyright and the works it protects.
Explain trademarks, deceptive similarity and conventional and non-conventional marks.
Identify geographical indications and their link with the origin of a product.

topics.title: Patent, design, plant variety and start-ups

concepts.learning_objective: State the criteria of patentability, the term of a patent and what cannot be patented.
Describe the protection given to designs, plant varieties and semiconductor layout designs.
State the objectives of the Startup India Scheme and the role of IPR for start-ups.

topics.title: Meaning and types of internal trade

concepts.learning_objective: Explain internal trade as buying and selling within a nation's boundaries, free of customs and import duty.
Distinguish wholesale trade from retail trade and explain why intermediaries are needed.

topics.title: Wholesale trade and services of wholesalers

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the nature of wholesale trade and the functions wholesalers perform in distribution.
Identify the services that wholesalers render to manufacturers.
Identify the services that wholesalers render to retailers.

topics.title: Retail trade and services of retailers

concepts.learning_objective: Explain that retailing is the sale of goods and services directly to ultimate consumers, however and wherever it is made.
Identify the services retailers render to manufacturers and wholesalers.
Identify the services retailers render to consumers.

topics.title: Itinerant retailers and fixed shop small retailers

concepts.learning_objective: Classify itinerant retailers such as hawkers, market traders, street traders and cheap jacks.
Describe fixed shop small retailers such as general stores, speciality shops, street stalls and second-hand shops.
Explain the features, advantages and limitations of departmental stores.
Explain the features, advantages and limitations of chain stores or multiple shops.
Compare departmental stores and multiple shops on location, range, services, pricing and customers.

topics.title: Mail order houses, consumer cooperative stores, super markets and vending machines

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how mail order houses work and which goods suit them.
Describe the formation, management, advantages and limitations of consumer cooperative stores.
Describe the working of super markets and vending machines and the goods they suit.
Explain GST as a destination-based tax with CGST, SGST, IGST and input tax credit.
State the key features of GST and the constitution and voting of the GST Council.

topics.title: Role of commerce and industry associations in promotion of internal trade

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why associations such as FICCI, CII and ASSOCHAM are formed and how they promote internal trade.
Identify the areas in which chambers of commerce and industry intervene with the government.

topics.title: Meaning of and reasons for international business

concepts.learning_objective: Define international business and explain why it is broader than international trade.
Explain how unequal resources and productivity lead nations to specialise and trade.
Distinguish between domestic and international business on the bases given in the chapter.
Explain how the use of different currencies and fluctuating exchange rates complicate international business.
Distinguish between merchandise (visible) trade and service (invisible) trade with examples.
Distinguish between foreign direct investment and portfolio investment.
Identify the benefits that international business offers to nations.
Identify the benefits that international business offers to business firms.
Distinguish direct from indirect exporting and state the advantages and limitations of exporting.
Explain contract manufacturing, its forms, advantages and limitations.

topics.title: Licensing, franchising, joint ventures and wholly owned subsidiaries

concepts.learning_objective: Explain licensing and franchising and distinguish between the two.
Explain the ways of forming a joint venture and its advantages and limitations.
Explain wholly owned subsidiaries and evaluate their suitability for a firm.
Arrange and explain the steps involved in a typical export transaction.
Identify the purpose of the main documents used in an export transaction.
Explain the steps involved in a typical import transaction into India.
Identify the purpose of the main documents used in an import transaction.
